label: prop:deuteron-fusion-frame
title: Fusion frame of the deuteron law: the $5$ is forced by $[2]_v^2 = [3]_v + 1$ and $g$ is the marginal-stability rate
html:
Let v = \sqrt{q_0} and write the symmetric q-integers

  [2]_v = v + v^{-1}, \qquad [3]_v = v^2 + 1 + v^{-2}.

The dimensionless content of the deuteron binding magnitude is fixed by three exact identities:

  1. (fusion) [2]_v^2 = [3]_v + 1 — the quantum-dimension form of the spin coupling \tfrac12 \otimes \tfrac12 = 1 \oplus 0;
  2. (the classical 5) 1 + [2]_v^2 = 5 + (v - v^{-1})^2, so the total quantum dimension of the two-nucleon channel decomposition is 5 at v = 1;
  3. (criticality) for the exchange rate g with g^2 = z^2/(1 + z^2) and z = [2]_v^{-1}, one has g^2\,(1 + [2]_v^2) = 1: the bond magnitude sits exactly at the marginal-stability point \det(1 + g\,M) = 0.

Rigidity of the integer 5

The bond factor z = 1/[2]_v is the Ocneanu–Markov normalization of the Hecke trace \mathrm{tr}_M (the same z that prop:three-strand-color-winding-rigidity and the reeb-flow magnitude use), not a modeling parameter. The quantity 1 + [2]_v^2 is the total quantum dimension of the two-nucleon channels \{V_0\ (\text{direct}),\ V_0 \oplus V_1\ (\text{fused})\}; by the fusion identity it equals 2 + [3]_v, whose classical value is 5. So the "5" in the near-match law B(^2\mathrm{H}) \approx 5g\,E_{\text{unit}} is a counting datum — a total quantum dimension — not an adjustable integer.

The exchange rate is a linking rate

The rate g = z/\sqrt{1+z^2} is the linking number per unit arc length, in exchange-cycle units, of a slope-z geodesic pair on the shared torus (the geometry-independent identity |\mathrm{Lk}|\cdot 2\pi r / L = g, verified symbolically and by Gauss integration). Composing the two facts, the deuteron magnitude reads canonical Markov parameter \to channel slope \to linking rate: the counting weight (rigid) times the geometric rate (deformed). Because the weight is topological, the trace-natural deformation of the classical 5 is 5g itself (the fully-deformed alternative (1 + [2]_v^2)\,g = 1/g splits from 5g by the exact factor 1 + (v-v^{-1})^2/5).

The archimedean evaluation at q_0 and the MeV unit E_{\text{unit}} are downstream and remain the open inputs of the linear law.
